text:
raj-support: Customer (AcmeCorp) opened an escalation — private VPC deployment intermittently failing inference streams. They see TLS handshake resets from our nodes ~50% of the time. Happening only from their on-prem NAT behind corporate firewall. Logs attached to ticket.

mia-sre: can you paste a short repro (curl/tcpdump) and which deployment (region, vpc-id)?

raj-support: repro steps from their infra team
1) connect to our endpoint behind their NAT: `curl -v https://private-infer.acme.redwood:443/health`
2) run a short streaming request and watch the client-side stream drop

They also ran: `openssl s_client -connect private-infer.acme.redwood:443 -alpn h2 -status -tls1_3` -> handshake sometimes completes, sometimes `read:errno=104`.

alex-eng: quick guess — sounds like ephemeral return-port exhaustion or NACL blocking ephemeral inbound responses. Do we know their VPC NACL and SG settings? (ask them for `aws ec2 describe-network-acls` and `describe-security-groups`)

raj-support: they've pasted security group rules: outbound TCP 443 allowed, inbound only control-plane ports. NACL is fairly strict: explicit DENY on ephemeral range except established allowed? they've got this: `100 allow TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0` and `200 deny ALL 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0` — they thought SG statefulness handled it.

mia-sre: aha — NACLs are stateless. If the NACL denies inbound ephemeral ranges, return packets from our service (which come back to ephemeral ports on their NAT) will be dropped. SG statefulness doesn't bypass NACL. That explains intermittent: depending on source port chosen by their NAT vs our SNAT port translation it sometimes lands in allowed range.

nat-security: can we get packet capture from their NAT/public egress? a `tcpdump` showing the 3-way handshake + reset would be ideal. Ask for `tcpdump -n -i eth0 tcp port 443 and host <our-eip>` and the server-side tcpdump too.

raj-support: they attached a pcap. excerpt:
```
11:02:12.123456 IP 10.10.10.5.51712 > 34.210.11.22.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
11:02:12.124010 IP 34.210.11.22.443 > 10.10.10.5.51712: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960, options [...]
11:02:12.124150 IP 10.10.10.5.51712 > 34.210.11.22.443: Flags [.], ack 1, win 64240, length 0
11:02:12.200000 IP 34.210.11.22.443 > 10.10.10.5.51712: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0, length 0
```

mia-sre: server sent R after handshake ack — that's interesting. Could be our load balancer/ALB or health layer resetting if it thinks connection not allowed or backend timing out. But combined with NACL deny it's consistent: sometimes backend can't finish migration of ports through NAT and connection looks unexpected.

alex-eng: on our side let's check the LB logs for TCP resets and our TLS timeouts. Also check if we are SNATing connections from our egress (dedicated infra) in a way that interacts with their NAT TTL. For private deployments: confirm their NAT gateway preserves source ports or if it randomizes above ephemeral ceiling. If their corporate firewall maps source ports into restricted high-range that NACL denies, it'd fail.

nat-security: recommended immediate workaround: ask them to open ephemeral inbound range on the NACL for return traffic (1024-65535) with rule number higher than deny, and ensure rule ordering permits ephemeral responses. Or add a specific allow for the NAT's chosen source-port-range if known.

raj-support: customer asked if we can mitigate from our side — any server changes?

mia-sre: short-term we can enable TCP keepalive and longer handshake timeouts on the LB to reduce races, but this won't fix an explicit stateless NACL deny. Long-term: recommend they replace deny-all ephemeral NACL with explicit allow for return ranges, or use a stateful firewall appliance that tracks sessions.

alex-eng: propose checklist for support reply:
- Ask customer to add NACL allow for ephemeral inbound ports 1024-65535 (or at least the 49152-65535 ephemeral range their NAT uses).
- Confirm SG allows ephemeral inbound? (SGs are stateful, but check no weird inbound-only rules).
- Provide tcpdump/pcap timestamps showing RSTs (we have server-side logs too) for correlation.
- Try reproducer with `curl --local-port 50000 -v` to see if using specific client port hit deny consistently.
- If they cannot change NACL, recommend using a NAT gateway that preserves ports or a managed proxy in their VPC.

raj-support: I'll send that checklist + pcap snippets and ask them to try enabling ephemeral allow. Also PM’ing @nat-security with the packet dump.

nat-security: thanks — after they update, ping me and we'll validate with `tcpdump` and LB logs. If they still see RSTs, we'll escalate to infra.

infra-bot: deploy-log: Checked LB (lb-priv-03) between 11:00-11:10: no backend TLS protocol errors, recorded 12 resets from source 10.10.10.5. Correlated with pcap times.

raj-support: closing loop — customer acknowledged and will change NACL rule to allow ephemeral inbound, will report back in ~1hr. :thumbsup:
